On Sat, Jan 10, 2026 at 10:03 AM lauren_bishop@redwood.com wrote:
> I've looped in Rishi (SDK) and Hiro (platform runtime) to triage immediately.

Quick triage notes — I reproduced a consistent failure locally using the pcap + a small harness that emulates connection churn (server side deliberately closes/warms a subset of sockets while streaming).

Observations:
- The SDK streaming parser's internal state machine assumes monotonic header-block delivery on resumed connections. When the TCP connection is torn and then resumed by the client, header continuation frames can arrive reordered relative to the parser's internal chunk state.
- In those cases the parser attempts to append continuation bytes to an already-committed header buffer, which then yields a malformed header sequence and a subsequent 503 from the runtime. It's effectively a state-drift in the streaming parser across connection handovers.
- This is more likely under heavy connection churn (your scale-up events) and with intermediate proxies that perform TCP fast-reconnect.

Reproducer summary (local):
1) Start SDK client harness (v1.4.1) pointed at a mock server.
2) Emit a long streaming response with interleaved header-continue frames.
3) Simulate connection reset mid-stream and immediately reestablish.
4) Parser sometimes mis-associates continuation bytes -> malformed header -> upstream 5xx.

Stack trace (snippet):
[parser.cpp:line 312] parse_continuation() assert(current_header_state == OPEN) failed
[stream_manager.cpp:line 218] on_frame() -> emit_error(HTTP_MALFORMED)

Short-term suggestion: add a parser-level guard to reset continuation state on connection resume if sequence numbers/stream IDs do not match expected monotonic progression. I'll push a minimal patch to v1.4.x that implements a safe fallback to reparse the current frame as an isolated header block.

I'll send the patch + unit tests in the next update. If we need immediate mitigation on your side: you can disable connection pooling/keep-alive for the client integration (this makes churn less likely) or route traffic to a Dedicated pool so transient reconnections are handled with more conservative timeouts.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior SDK Engineer, Redwood Inference

Update from runtime side (root-cause & fix plan):

Root cause: when a streaming TCP connection is broken and quickly reestablished, some intermediary stacks (LBs/proxies) will re-sequence frames in a way that violates the parser's assumption about header continuation ordering. The parser does not aggressively validate per-stream sequence tokens on resume, so continuation bytes can be appended into an already finalised header buffer. This causes header parsing to fail and then the runtime returns a 503/HTTP_MALFORMED.

Proposed fixes:
- SDK hotfix (v1.4.2): on connection resume, validate stream/continuation sequence markers. If mismatch detected, reset continuation state and re-parse the pending bytes as a fresh header block. Patch attached: sdk-hotfix-diff.patch
- Server-side hardening: make the runtime tolerant of malformed header attempts by returning a 400 to the client instead of an upstream 5xx and log a structured event for analysis.
- E2E test: add a controlled connection-churn harness in our CI that simulates quick reconnects and verifies parser invariants.

Rollout plan:
- Patch built + unit tests (24 hrs).
- Canary release to 5 customers (48 hrs).
- Full rollout and notify customers (72 hrs).

I'll coordinate the PR and tag the exact canary customers; Greystone will be offered early canary if you permit it.

— Hiro
